title: Return Values
objective: Send a value back from a function with return and use it in the caller.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A function that only prints hands its output straight to the screen — nothing comes back to the code that called it. return sends a value back instead, so the caller can store it, check it, or pass it somewhere else.
As soon as Python executes a return statement, the function stops immediately — any code after it in that function never runs, even if it's still indented inside the function body.

A function without an explicit return statement returns None, Python's way of saying 'nothing.' Printing and returning solve different problems: printing is for showing a human something right now; returning is for handing a value to the rest of the program.
explanation.rule: return sends a value back to the caller and immediately ends the function — code after it never runs.

examples.title: Using a Returned Value
examples.code:
def double(n):
    return n * 2

result = double(21)
print(result)
examples.note: double() hands back a value, which is stored in result and used afterward — it never prints anything itself.

options: It always runs after the return statements.
It never runs — both branches return before reaching it.
It runs only when n is negative.

feedback.correct: Correct — return exits the function immediately, so unreachable code after it never executes.
feedback.incorrect: return ends the function right away. Any code after a return that always executes first is unreachable.

assignment.title: Temper the Blade
assignment.brief: Write temper_rating(hardness) that returns 'brittle' if hardness > 60, 'tempered' if hardness >= 30, otherwise 'soft'. Print the returned value for temper_rating(45).
requirements: Define temper_rating(hardness) using return, not print, inside the function.
Cover all three cases with if/elif/else.
Print temper_rating(45) at the top level.
assignment.starterCode:
def temper_rating(hardness):
    # Return the correct rating string; do not print inside this function.
    pass

print(temper_rating(45))
assignment.testHarness:
# ---- Code Forge validation ----
import io, contextlib
_cf_buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(_cf_buf):
    print(temper_rating(45))
_cf_result = _cf_buf.getvalue()
print("__CF_TEST_OUTPUT__")
print(repr(_cf_result))

hints: Use return inside the function instead of print.
45 is not greater than 60, but it is >= 30, so it should return 'tempered'.
The print() call at the bottom is what displays the returned value.
Make sure every branch of the if/elif/else uses return, not print.
